text: Where are the Harlem Park Three now? HBO's When a Witness Recants. The Harlem Park Three, Alfred Chestnut, Ransom Watkins and Andrew Stewart, were freed on Nov. 25, 2019, after 36 years in prison for a 1983 Baltimore killing they did not commit. Maryland awarded each man about $2.9 million in 2020, and Baltimore agreed in October 2023 to pay $48 million to settle their lawsuit.. HBO's documentary "When a Witness Recants," about the Harlem Park Three, premieres on Nov. 17, 2026.. The three were arrested on Nov. 24, 1983, at age 16, after a 14-year-old student was killed at Harlem Park Junior High School in Baltimore, and were convicted on May 28, 1984, and sentenced to life. Their convictions rested on testimony from teenage witnesses that the documentary says was coerced. Their release in 2019 followed the discovery of police reports that had been withheld; Baltimore City Circuit Judge Charles Peters freed them. In August 2020 the men sued the Baltimore Police Department and officers who worked the case. The city's Board of Estimates approved the $48 million settlement on Oct. 18, 2023; each man was to receive about $14.9 million. Their story is the subject of "When a Witness Recants," directed by Dawn Porter, with Ta-Nehisi Coates as an executive producer. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on Jan. 27, 2026, is based on a New Yorker story by Jennifer Gonnerman, and debuts on HBO Max on Nov. 17, 2026.

How are Grammy nominations decided? 2027 nominees out Nov. 16. Grammy nominations are decided by a vote of the Recording Academy's voting members. After experts screen entries for eligibility, members vote in a first round, and the top vote-getters become nominees; accounting firm Deloitte counts the ballots. For the 2027 Grammys, nominations will be announced on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026.. The Recording Academy announces nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026.. Each voting member may vote in up to 10 categories across up to three genre fields, plus all six General Field categories, such as Album, Record and Song of the Year. Members are told to vote only in fields where they are peers of the nominees. A "Ballot Plus" option lets some members vote in extra categories where they actively work. In craft categories, such as engineering and packaging, final nominations are chosen by special committees of members who work in that craft. Screening sessions with more than 350 experts check only that entries are eligible and in the right category; the Academy says they do not judge artistic quality. For the 2027 awards, the eligibility period ran from Aug. 31, 2025, to Aug. 28, 2026, and first-round voting took place Oct. 12-22, 2026. Final-round voting runs from Dec. 10, 2026, to Jan. 7, 2027. The 69th Grammy Awards will be held on Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and will air on ABC, Disney+ and Hulu.

Is I Play Rocky a true story? How Stallone got Rocky made. Yes. "I Play Rocky" is based on the true story of how a young, unknown Sylvester Stallone fought to get "Rocky" made in the 1970s and to star in it himself. Anthony Ippolito plays Stallone. Directed by Peter Farrelly, the film opened in limited release on Nov. 6, 2026, and expands nationwide on Nov. 20.. "I Play Rocky" expands to theaters nationwide on Nov. 20, 2026, after a limited release on Nov. 6.. Amazon MGM Studios says Stallone was "told 'no' at every turn" but held firm on playing the lead role. "Rocky" was released in 1976, nearly 50 years before this film. Peter Gamble wrote the script, and the movie premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sept. 12, 2026. The cast plays real people from the making of "Rocky": AnnaSophia Robb as Stallone's wife, Sasha Czack; Matt Dillon as his father, Frank Stallone Sr.; P.J. Byrne and Toby Kebbell as producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff; Jay Duplass as director John G. Avildsen; Stephan James as Carl Weathers; Kiki Seto as Talia Shire; Robert Morgan as Burgess Meredith; and Scot Teller as Burt Young. Rob Demery plays boxer Joe Frazier, and Tracy Letts also appears. Farrelly won the Oscar for best picture for "Green Book." The film is distributed by Amazon MGM Studios.

Is Leonida a real place? GTA 6's fictional Florida, explained. No. Leonida is a fictional U.S. State created by Rockstar Games for Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is based on Florida. Its main city, Vice City, is the series' long-running version of Miami. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on Nov. 19, 2026.. Grand Theft Auto VI, set in the fictional state of Leonida, is scheduled for release on Nov. 19, 2026.. Rockstar has named several regions of Leonida. Vice City is billed as the "sun and fun capital" of America. The Leonida Keys are a tropical island chain that resembles the Florida Keys, and Grassrivers is a swampy area that appears modeled on the Everglades. Port Gellhorn is described as Leonida's forgotten coast of cheap motels and closed-down attractions, Ambrosia is home to a sugar refinery and a local biker gang, and Mount Kalaga sits on the state's northern border. The name follows the series' habit of renaming real places: GTA V's San Andreas is a fictional version of Southern California, and Los Santos stands in for Los Angeles. Vice City first appeared in the original Grand Theft Auto in 1997 and was the setting of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City in 2002. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, reaffirmed the Nov. 19, 2026, release date during an investor call in May 2026.

Is The Altruists a true story? Netflix's FTX series, explained. Yes. Netflix's "The Altruists" dramatizes the real rise and fall of the crypto exchange FTX, focusing on founder Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, former CEO of Alameda Research. Anthony Boyle plays Bankman-Fried and Julia Garner plays Ellison. The eight-episode limited series premieres on Netflix on Nov. 19, 2026.. Netflix releases "The Altruists," its limited series about the FTX collapse, on Nov. 19, 2026.. The series draws on reporting by Kevin T. Dugan and Jen Wieczner for New York magazine. Graham Moore, the Oscar-winning writer of "The Imitation Game," created it and is showrunner with Jacqueline Hoyt. Barack and Michelle Obama's Higher Ground Productions is among the producers. The cast also includes Paul Reiser and Robin Weigert as Bankman-Fried's parents, Joe Bankman and Barbara Fried, Matt Rife as Ryan Salame, Karan Soni as Nishad Singh and Eugene Young as Gary Wang. In real life, a New York jury found Bankman-Fried guilty on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy in 2023, and Judge Lewis Kaplan sentenced him to 25 years in prison on March 28, 2024. A federal appeals court upheld his conviction on June 12, 2026. Ellison pleaded guilty, testified against him and was sentenced to two years in prison on Sept. 24, 2024.

Who is Carter Faith? Heartland actress and CMA new artist nominee. Carter Faith is a country singer-songwriter from Davidson, North Carolina, signed to MCA Nashville. Her debut album, "Cherry Valley," came out on Oct. 3, 2025. She is nominated for New Artist of the Year at the CMA Awards on Nov. 18, 2026, and she co-stars in Netflix's thriller Heartland, out Nov. 13.. Faith appears in Netflix's Heartland, out Nov. 13, 2026, and is a nominee at the CMA Awards on Nov. 18, 2026.. Faith, born Carter Faith Jones in 2000, studied in Belmont University's songwriting program in Nashville and graduated in December 2021. She made her Grand Ole Opry debut in June 2022. Before her debut album she released the EPs "Let Love Be Love" (2021), "Man" (2023) and "The Aftermath" (2024). Singles include "Betty" and "That's When You Know," a 2026 collaboration with Kygo. "Cherry Valley" was nominated for Album of the Year at the 61st Academy of Country Music Awards in 2026, making her the first artist in more than a decade to earn that nomination with a debut album. At the 2026 CMA Awards she is a first-time nominee, competing for New Artist of the Year with Avery Anna, Emily Ann Roberts, Tucker Wetmore and Stephen Wilson Jr. In Netflix's Heartland she plays Charlie Heart, a rising country musician who goes missing; Jessica Chastain plays her aunt, a retired country star who searches for her.

Who is in the cast of Heartland on Netflix? Jessica Chastain leads. Netflix's Heartland stars Jessica Chastain as Misty Jones, a retired country music star who comes out of seclusion to search for her missing niece. The cast also includes Garrett Hedlund, country singer Carter Faith, Ross Lynch, Jennifer Nettles and John Hawkes. The thriller streams on Netflix worldwide from Nov. 13, 2026.. Heartland premieres on Netflix on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026.. Shana Feste, the writer-director of "Country Strong," directed and co-wrote the film. Netflix lists these roles: Jessica Chastain as Misty Jones, Garrett Hedlund as Roy Combs, Carter Faith as Charlie Heart, Ross Lynch as Jace, Jennifer Nettles as Winnie Jo Lean, John Hawkes as Clark and Skyler Day as Lea Heart. Ben Dickey, Isabelle Kusman, Wynn Everett, Paul Sparks, David Rysdahl, Hill Harper and Norbert Leo Butz also appear. The story is set in Nashville. Misty's search for her niece, a rising country musician, leads her into the city's darker side and forces her to confront her own past. Netflix lists the running time as 1 hour 54 minutes. Peter Chernin and Jenno Topping of Chernin Entertainment are among the producers. Two of the actors are working country artists: Jennifer Nettles is the singer of Sugarland, and Carter Faith, who plays Charlie Heart, is a 2026 CMA Awards nominee for New Artist of the Year.

How is the Senate majority leader chosen? A secret party vote. The Senate majority leader is not elected by the full Senate. Senators of the majority party pick their leader in a closed party conference, by secret ballot when the race is contested, and the winner needs a majority of the votes cast. The Constitution does not mention the post. After the 2026 midterms, the Democratic vote is expected in early December.. Democrats won control of the Senate in the Nov. 3, 2026, midterms, and some Democratic Senate candidates have said they will not back Chuck Schumer for leader.. Under the Senate Democratic Conference's rules, leadership elections can be held no earlier than December before a new Congress begins, or whenever a vacancy occurs. Contested races are decided by secret ballot and must be held in person; voting continues until one candidate wins a majority of members present and voting, and with more than two candidates the lowest finisher drops off after each ballot. No vote of the full Senate is needed to confirm the result. On Nov. 4, 2026, Chuck Schumer said, "I'll be reelected as majority leader," Roll Call reported. Roll Call said Democrats would hold 54 to 56 seats and that the leadership vote, which includes senators-elect, will likely happen in early December. Roll Call also reported that several Democratic Senate candidates, including Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan and Illinois' Juliana Stratton, have said they would not back Schumer. The new Congress, and the new Senate majority, begins on Jan. 3, 2027. The majority leader sets the Senate's floor schedule and decides which bills come up for a vote.

Who has the most MVP awards in MLB history? Bonds, then Ohtani. Barry Bonds has the most MVP awards in MLB history with seven (1990, 1992, 1993 and 2001-2004). Shohei Ohtani is second with four (2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025). Ohtani is a 2026 NL MVP finalist, and the winners will be announced on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026.. MLB announces the 2026 AL and NL MVP winners on Nov. 12, 2026; Ohtani is a finalist for a fifth MVP.. Eleven players have won exactly three MVP awards, according to MLB.com: Aaron Judge (2022, 2024, 2025), Mike Trout (2014, 2016, 2019), Albert Pujols (2005, 2008, 2009), Alex Rodriguez (2003, 2005, 2007), Mike Schmidt (1980, 1981, 1986), Mickey Mantle (1956, 1957, 1962), Yogi Berra (1951, 1954, 1955), Roy Campanella (1951, 1953, 1955), Stan Musial (1943, 1946, 1948), Joe DiMaggio (1939, 1941, 1947) and Jimmie Foxx (1932, 1933, 1938). Ohtani has won the MVP in each of the past three seasons. He and Frank Robinson are the only players to win MVP in both leagues, and Ohtani is the only one with more than one MVP in each league. The 2026 NL finalists are Ohtani, Pete Crow-Armstrong (Cubs) and Brice Turang (Brewers). The AL finalists are Yordan Alvarez (Astros), Junior Caminero (Rays) and Bobby Witt Jr. (Royals). The MVP is voted on by the Baseball Writers' Association of America, and ballots are cast before the postseason begins.

Has a rookie ever won the Cy Young? Yes, Fernando Valenzuela in 1981. Yes. Fernando Valenzuela of the Los Angeles Dodgers won both the NL Cy Young Award and NL Rookie of the Year in 1981, and he remains the only pitcher in MLB history to win both in the same season. In 2026, Guardians lefty Parker Messick is a finalist for both AL Rookie of the Year and the AL Cy Young.. Parker Messick is a finalist for AL Rookie of the Year (announced Nov. 9, 2026) and the AL Cy Young (Nov. 11, 2026).. Valenzuela went 13-7 with a 2.48 ERA in the strike-shortened 1981 season. He opened the year 8-0 with five shutouts and a 0.50 ERA, setting off "Fernandomania," and the Dodgers went on to win the 1981 World Series. He died in October 2024 at age 63. The 2026 AL Rookie of the Year finalists are Kevin McGonigle (Tigers), Parker Messick (Guardians) and Payton Tolle (Red Sox). The AL Cy Young finalists are Dylan Cease (Blue Jays), Parker Messick (Guardians) and Cam Schlittler (Yankees). Rookie of the Year will be announced on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, and the Cy Young on Wednesday, Nov. 11. Both awards are voted on by members of the Baseball Writers' Association of America, with ballots submitted before the postseason starts.
